description: Bremen Zwei freut sich auf Steffen Möller, Anna Osius, Sebastian Krumbiegel und Pasquale Aleardi.
headings: Live-Talks in Bremen – jetzt anmelden und Plätze sichern
text: Live-Gäste von Bremen Zwei - Radio Bremen Zur Hauptnavigation Zum Inhalt Zur Fußzeile Barrierefrei Livestream Hilfe Suche Suche starten Suche Menü Hauptmenü Schließen Programm Dialog Medienkompetenz Über uns Karriere Kontakt Suche Suche starten Barrierefrei Livestream Hilfe Startseite Pressemitteilungen Live-Gäste von Bremen Zwei Standdatum: 7. August 2026 . Live-Gäste von Bremen Zwei Datum: 29. August bis 19. September 2026, 11.05 Uhr | Theater Bremen und Bremen Zwei Bremen Zwei präsentiert wieder die Talk-Reihe Live-Gäste. Katrin Krämer und Tom Grote freuen sich auf besondere Geschichten, unerwartete Einblicke und erfrischende Analysen – Gespräche mit Witz und Niveau live im Theater Bremen und auf Bremen Zwei. Der Eintritt ist frei, die Zahl der Plätze begrenzt – Online-Anmeldung unter bremenzwei.de. Seite teilen Per E-Mail versenden Radio Bremen bei Google bevorzugen Bild: Nicole Giese/Tapete Records/ARD/Patrick Grzybowski | Montage Radio Bremen Live-Talks in Bremen – jetzt anmelden und Plätze sichern Bremen Zwei lädt zu Live-Talks in das Foyer des Kleinen Hauses des Theaters Bremen ein: mit Musiker Sebastian Krumbiegel, ARD-Korrespondentin Anna Osius, Schauspieler Pasquale Aleardi und Kabarettist Steffen Möller. bremenzwei.de Steffen Möller Den Auftakt macht am 29. August Steffen Möller . Ein Sprachkurs in Krakau hat das Leben des früheren Deutschlehrers verändert. Dort hat er sich in Polen verliebt, und so begann eine unerwartete und verblüffende Karriere. Anfang der 2000er Jahre avancierte Möller als deutscher Kartoffelbauer in einer erfolgreichen Seifenoper zum TV-Star in Polen. Heute gilt er als der humorvollste Brückenbauer zwischen Deutschland und seinem Nachbarn im Osten. Der Kabarettist und Bestsellerautor pendelt zwischen beiden Ländern und arbeitet auch in Zeiten politischer Konflikte zwischen Berlin und Warschau unverdrossen an einer besseren Verständigung zwischen den Nachbarn. Anna Osius Anna Osius kam kurz nach dem Arabischen Frühling zum ersten Mal als ARD-Korrespondentin in Ägyptens Hauptstadt Kairo. Seitdem ist viel passiert, nicht nur in der "Stadt der 1000 Minarette", sondern in der gesamten arabischen Welt. Mittlerweile berichtet Anna Osius aus 15 Ländern über die Lage im Nahen und Mittleren Osten. Für ihre Reportagen wurde sie mehrfach ausgezeichnet, unter anderem mit dem Axel-Springer-Preis, dem CNN Journalist Award und dem Civis Preis. Besonders wichtig ist ihr, auch die Geschichten jenseits von Gewalt und Krieg zu erzählen und den Menschen ein Gesicht zu geben. Welche Menschen ihr dabei besonders nahegekommen sind, kann sie als Bremen Zwei-Live-Gast am 5. September erzählen. Sebastian Krumbiegel Wie Musikunterricht ein ganzes Leben prägen kann, davon weiß Sebastian Krumbiegel , Bremen Zwei-Live-Gast am 12. September , ein Lied zu singen. Die Grundlagen für die Karriere des Musikers wurden im berühmten Leipziger Thomaner-Chor gelegt. Seinem inneren Kompass ist Krumbiegel schon damals zu DDR-Zeiten gefolgt. Mit seinem Widerspruchsgeist eckte er an im strengen Chor-Internat, wo das Leben auf Disziplin getrimmt war. Nach der Wiedervereinigung gaben sich Krumbiegel und seine ehemaligen Mitschüler einen neuen Namen: Aus den "Herzbuben" wurden "Die Prinzen". Der Beginn einer beispiellosen Erfolgsgeschichte mit zahlreichen Ohrwürmern. Aber auch als Solomusiker ist Krumbiegel aktiv, genauso wie als politisch engagierter Künstler in Zeiten des Rechtsrucks. Naheliegend also, dass sein aktuelles Album den Titel "Kompass" trägt. Pasquale Aleardi Letzter Bremen Zwei Live-Gast am 19. September ist ein Schweizer mit griechisch-italienischen Wurzeln. Zum Star im deutschen Fernsehen aber machte ihn die Rolle eines französischen Polizisten: Pasquale Aleardi ist international gut aufgestellt. Den Pariser Kommissar Dupin, den es wider Willen in die Bretagne verschlägt, spielt er so überzeugend, dass sogar Franzosen diese deutsche Serie gerne gucken. So schwer man ihn auf eine Nationalität festlegen kann, so vielseitig gibt er sich auch beruflich, spielt in deutschen Komödien genauso wie im US-Blockbuster oder am Broadway. Und tourt neben der Schauspielerei noch als Musiker. "Die Phonauten" heißt seine Band, ihre unterhaltsamen Eigenkompositionen nennt sie "Antidepressionsmusik". Beste Voraussetzungen also für einen unterhaltsamen Vormittag mit einem Entertainer, den die Presse wechselweise als "heißblütigen Latino" und "charmanten Kerl von nebenan" feiert. title: How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services – Privacy & Terms – Google
headings: How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services
How you can control the information collected by Google on these sites and apps
text: How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services – Privacy & Terms – Google Skip to main content Privacy & Terms Privacy & Terms Sign in Overview Privacy Policy Terms of Service Technologies FAQ Privacy & Terms Overview Privacy Policy Terms of Service Technologies Advertising How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services How Google uses cookies How Google uses location information How Google uses credit card numbers for payments How Google Voice works Google Product Privacy Guide How Google retains data we collect FAQ Privacy & Terms Privacy & Terms Privacy & Terms Overview Privacy Policy Terms of Service Technologies FAQ Google Account Technologies Advertising How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services How Google uses cookies How Google uses location information How Google uses credit card numbers for payments How Google Voice works Google Product Privacy Guide How Google retains data we collect How Google uses information from sites or apps that use our services Many websites and apps use Google services to improve their content and keep it free. When they integrate our services, these sites and apps share information with Google. For example, when you visit a website that uses advertising services like AdSense or Google Ads, including analytics tools like Google Analytics, or embeds video content from YouTube, your web browser automatically sends certain information to Google. This includes the URL of the page you’re visiting and your IP address. We may use the IP address, for example, to identify your general location, to measure the effectiveness of ads, and, depending on your settings, to improve the relevance of the ads you see. We may also set cookies on your browser or read cookies that are already there. Apps that use Google advertising services also share information with Google, such as the name of the app and a unique identifier for advertising. Google uses the information shared by sites and apps to deliver our services, maintain and improve them, develop new services, measure the effectiveness of advertising, protect against fraud and abuse, and personalize content and ads you see on Google and on our partners’ sites and apps. See our Privacy Policy to learn more about how we process data for each of these purposes and our Advertising page for more about Google ads, how your information is used in the context of advertising, and how long Google stores this information. Our Privacy Policy explains the legal grounds Google relies upon to process your information — for example, we may process your information with your consent or to pursue legitimate interests such as providing, maintaining and improving our services to meet the needs of our users. Sometimes, when processing information shared with us by sites and apps, those sites and apps will ask for your consent before allowing Google to process your information. For example, a banner may appear on a site asking for consent for Google to process the information that site collects. When that happens, we will respect the purposes described in the consent you give to the site or app, rather than the legal grounds described in the Google Privacy Policy. If you want to change or withdraw your consent, you should visit the site or app in question to do so. Ad personalization If ad personalization is turned on, Google will use your information to make your ads more useful for you. For example, a website that sells mountain bikes might use Google's ad services. After you visit that site, you could see an ad for mountain bikes on a different site that shows ads served by Google. If ad personalization is off, Google will not collect or use your information to create an ad profile or personalize the ads Google shows to you. You will still see ads, but they may not be as useful. Ads may still be based on the topic of the website or app you're looking at, your current search terms, or on your general location, but not on your interests, search history, or browsing history. Your information can still be used for the other purposes mentioned above, such as to measure the effectiveness of advertising and protect against fraud and abuse. When you interact with a website or app that uses Google services, you may be asked to choose whether you want to see personalized ads from ad providers, including Google. Regardless of your choice, Google will not personalize the ads you see if your ad personalization setting is off or your account is ineligible for personalized ads. You can see and control what information we use to show you ads by visiting your ad settings . How you can control the information collected by Google on these sites and apps Here are some of the ways you can control the information that is shared by your device when you visit or interact with sites and apps that use Google services: Ad Settings helps you control ads you see on Google services (such as Google Search or YouTube), or on non-Google websites and apps that use Google ad services. You can also learn how ads are personalized, opt out of ad personalization, and block specific advertisers. If you are signed in to your Google Account, and depending on your Account settings, My Activity allows you to review and control data that is saved as history by your activity controls when you use Google services, which may include information we collect from the sites and apps you have visited. You can browse by date and by topic, and delete part or all of your saved activity. Many websites and apps use Google Analytics to understand how visitors engage with their sites or apps. If you don’t want Analytics to be used in your browser, you can install the Google Analytics browser add-on . Learn more about Google Analytics and privacy . Incognito mode in Chrome allows you to limit the information Chrome saves to your device when you browse the web. Learn more about Incognito . Cookies are deleted after you've closed all of your incognito windows and tabs, and your bookmarks and settings are stored until you delete them. Learn more about cookies . Using Incognito mode in Chrome or other private browsing modes does not prevent the collection of data when you visit websites that use Google services, and Google still collects data when you visit websites using Google services in private browsing modes. Many browsers, including Chrome, allow you to block third-party cookies. You can also clear any existing cookies from within your browser. Learn more about managing cookies in Chrome . Videos with these audio tracks are marked as “auto-dubbed” in the video description. Viewers can indicate their preferred languages for audio, titles and descriptions, or they can switch between the original and dubbed audio tracks for any specific video. When you upload a new video, dubs will be automatically generated. These dubs will be published according to your publication settings . Over time, we may also generate dubs for previously published videos. Eligibility This feature is enabled by default for eligible creators. If you don’t have automatic dubbing enabled, you can use early access to enable it by clicking Enable in “ Advanced settings .” Your video may be ineligible for automatic dubbing due to the following reasons: Video Length: The video exceeds 120 minutes. Audio Content: The video contains no speech, only music, or very little spoken content. The original audio is in a language we do not currently support. Source Language Detection: We were unable to automatically detect the source language of the original audio. Speech Pacing: The speech in the original audio is too fast, which would result in an unlistenable, sped-up dub. Copyright Claims: The video contains copyrighted content . Automatic dubbing best practices To generate more accurate dubs, confirm you have accurately set your original video or channel language to the correct language when you upload the video. If your video's default language is set incorrectly, its automatic dubs may be mistranslated. You cannot edit automatic dubs. If your automatic dubs were mistranslated, you can update the original video language to the correct language and the dubs will be automatically generated again. Automatic dubbing quality Automatic dubbing helps make information more accessible globally. Over time, dubs may be regenerated to improve the quality, and the quality may not be the same across all languages. Some languages may support expressive speech, which replicates the original speaker's pitch and intonation to produce more natural-sounding dubs. Dubs are generated automatically, so they might contain errors due to mispronunciations, accents, dialects, or background noise in the original video. We may also have challenges translating proper nouns, idioms, and jargon. Other issues may arise with speech recognition, like difficulty matching the voice used for dubbing to the original voice. Available languages Note: We are gradually expanding support for new languages and improving dub quality. As a result, some channels might have access to new languages sooner. For a specific video, you can refer to the Languages page in YouTube Studio for a list of languages available for that video, including which are experimental. Supported languages for automatic dubbing Original language Language(s) available for automatic dubbing Arabic English* Bengali English* Chinese English Chinese (Traditional) English Dutch English English Arabic, Bengali, Dutch, French*, German*, Hebrew, Hindi*, Indonesian*, Italian*, Japanese, Korean, Malayalam, Polish, Portuguese*, Punjabi, Russian, Spanish*, Tamil, Telugu, Ukrainian Farsi English French English* German English* Hebrew English Hindi Bengali, English* Indonesian English* Italian English* Japanese English Korean English* or Indonesian Malayalam English Polish English Portuguese English*, Spanish Punjabi English Romanian English Russian English* Spanish Arabic, English*, Portuguese Swahili English Tamil English Telugu English* Thai English Turkish English Ukrainian English* Urdu English Vietnamese English Note: Languages marked with an asterisk (*) support expressive speech, which replicates the original audio's pitch and intonation to produce more natural-sounding dubs. However, even if a language supports expressive speech, it won’t always be used. Turn on or off automatic dubbing for your channel You can turn on or off auto-dubbing at any time. Open the YouTube Studio app . Tap your profile picture . Tap Settings . Under Content , tap Automatic dubbing . Turn automatic dubbing on or off. If you would like to review the dubs before they’re published, tap Publish manually . Adjust automatic dubbing publication settings To review automatically generated dubs before they are published (or to prevent their publication), enable the manual review option within your channel settings. Open the YouTube Studio app . Tap your profile picture . Tap Settings . Under Content , tap Automatic dubbing . Tap Publish manually to review the dubs before they’re published. Lip sync Lip sync is an automatic dubbing feature that alters the speaker's lip movement to align with the dubbed audio. Note: Early access to this experimental feature is available to select channels, and only supports qualifying videos and languages. Manage lip sync settings Sign in to YouTube Studio on your computer. Click Settings Channel Advanced settings . Ensure the Allow automatic dubbing box is checked, to make the lip sync options visible. Check the Allow experimental lip sync box to experiment with the feature on your dubs. If the setting does not appear then your channel does not currently have access to the experimental lip sync feature. Click Save . Manage automatic dubbing for a video Note: Managing dubs—including previewing, publishing, or deleting—is only available via YouTube Studio on your computer. Preview dubs Sign in to YouTube Studio on your computer. Click Content , then select the video you want to manage dubbing for. Click Languages . In the “Language” column, click on the relevant language. In the “Preview” menu under the video, select the relevant language. Play the video. Review dub transcript Sign in to YouTube Studio on your computer. Click Content , then select the video you want to manage dubbing for. Click Languages . In the “Language” column, click on the relevant language. In the “Audio” row under the description section, select the relevant language. Click on the to show the dubbed audio options menu. Click on “Review” to show the transcript. Publish, unpublish, or delete dubs For dubs that are not automatically published, you have to publish the dubs manually. Sign in to YouTube Studio on your computer. Click Content , then select the video you want to manage dubbing for. Click Languages . Hover over the relevant language, then click in the “Audio” column. Select Publish , Unpublish , or Delete . Note: When you unpublish a dub, you can choose to republish it or delete it later. The dub will no longer be available for viewers after it has been unpublished. Once a dub is deleted, it won’t be available and you can’t republish it. Was this helpful? How can we improve it? title: diamond geezer
text: diamond geezer diamond geezer Sunday, September 06, 2026 Life viewed from London E3 An extraordinary thing is happening tomorrow on Stroudley Walk , a new cafe is opening! We've had fried chicken for a while and a juice bar gave it a go after lockdown, but this is the first time there's been a sitdowner with macchiatos, croissants, hash browns and lasagne. It's called Minnie's Coffee and Food and it made me double-take. It lurks underneath Zellie Emerson House, one of four new housing blocks hereabouts, in a small unit I'd assumed would stay uneconomically empty. Instead our local social housing company have hired out the space as part of their HARCA Café Collective, "an initiative making quality food and drink accessible and affordable to residents and visitors across Bow and Poplar". It's not clear whether Minnie is the owner's name or a reference to Minnie Lansbury the East End suffragette, but given the estate's history and thematic rebrand I'd assume the latter. Apart from the obvious hot drinks the menu also includes breakfast options (until 11am), snacks and a limited range of lunches. I can't remember the last time anywhere round here did a genuine cooked breakfast, and OK there's no bacon but £8 is a pretty good deal. As for lunches each day of the week brings a single meat or vegetarian choice (Mondays curried, Tuesdays stir-fried, Wednesdays filo royale, Thursdays lasagne and Fridays crispy with potato wedges), also soup, also foccacia-based sandwiches, also six quid salads. And yes I know you've probably had this round your way for ages but this is Stroudley Walk for heaven's sake, a culinary dead end since time immemorial. Like most modern food outlets they've not bothered with a website just an Instagram account nobody would ever think to search for. Unnervingly the first post said "Almost ready to serve you!" and that was in June. Also their tagline is "More than just coffee, we’re a community" which I reckon is wilfully unproven given they haven't opened yet. But opening day is Monday at 7.30am and to celebrate they've got a special offer of 50% OFF ALL HOT DRINKS UNTIL MIDDAY. I live nearby and have a kettle so not even Builders Tea for 75p is going to tempt me in, but I wish Minnie well as gentrification finally sparks to life in Stroudley Walk . It's what the incomers who've paid half a million to live in the tower nextdoor have been waiting for, indeed long expected. posted 07:30 : 30 unblogged things I did in September 1986 They didn't have blogs or the internet forty years ago, so here are 30 things I didn't digitally publish at the time. To help you get your bearings I was 21, teetering between university and a job, so chose to delay things by undertaking an extra year's study up north. Mon 1: Sign on at the dole office, but am called to one side to undergo a random check. Thankfully they weren't tough checks in those days. [On TV: London Plus with John Stapleton] Tue 2: My university tutor pops up on Radio 1 Newsbeat talking about vaccinated chickens. Get a phone call inviting me to a job interview on Friday but turn them down because I've decided oil economics isn't for me. Wed 3: Have to go for a job-related medical. Worried it might be a full strip-off but it's no worse than filling a bottle and getting my blood pressure checked. [The supervising medic was called Dr Doodoo] Thu 4: Two friends from university drive over and meet the tortoise, then we go for a walk round Ruislip Lido, watch the water skiing and have cheeseburgers in Wimpy. [Ooh look, I have a photo] Fri 5: My dad takes the morning off work but the man from Anglian Windows never turns up to do the survey and I have rarely heard him so cross. Sat 6: Wimbledon FC beat Watford 1-0 to stay top of Division 1, so I annoy my brother by putting a Womble on the doorstep when he gets home from the match. [On TV: Episode 1 of the season-long Doctor Who story, Trial of a Time Lord] Sun 7: Mum and Dad are debating where to go for a silver wedding getaway next month [it turns out to be a cottage near a radar station in Norfolk] Mon 8: University friend returns and drives us down to the Odeon Marble Arch to watch Aliens. Thoroughly enjoy. [Alas moving up north will squash this budding friendship] [A quick check online and I see he's just retired from his top job in the City] Tue 9: When our nextdoor neighbour moved out she gave us £40 to go out for a family meal, so tonight we go to the Ponderosa Steak House in Watford High Street, a legendary venue. I have sirloin steak and they forget to offer us any free refills. Wed 10: Buy a £299 Sony hi-fi from Tottenham Court Road and nearly collapse lugging it home on the tube. Thu 11: For my 'final' meal Mum cooks roast lamb (washed down with a bottle of Riesling) and lemon meringue pie. [nobody has ever made lemon meringue pie as well as my Mum did] Fri 12: A very long drive up the A1 with the boot full of boxes. This time I've split it into separate bits so you can pick and choose. Past, Present and Future The 349 was introduced in 2004 to strengthen bus capacity down the old A10, aka the High Road, as Ken Livingstone expanded the network. It's now being removed because that capacity isn't needed and times are tight, along with other cuts and tweaks as TfL take a small axe to services in the upper Lea Valley. If you're heading south currently the 279 starts at Waltham Cross, the 349 joins in at Ponders End, the 149 and 259 are added at Edmonton Green, then the 476, 243 and 76 feed in through Tottenham. The plan is for the 259 to nudge back to Ponders End to fill in the gap left by the 349 and also for the 279 to switch to Stamford Hill at the southern end, all starting tomorrow. In separate plans the 149 will be whisked away later. No journeys become impossible as a result of any of this, you might just have to wait longer for a fuller bus. Bus Geekery The 349 is currently one of the contenders for London's straightest bus route. It has a right turn just after the first stop and a left turn just before the last stop, but everything else is straight up (or down) the High Road. That's 94% of the route on the same road (even if that road's not perfectly straight). Other contenders for the title include the 32 ( 93% along Watling Street with a short bend at either end) and the 116 ( 91% , wrecked only by the pedestrianisation of Hounslow High Street). From this weekend the 279 will also be 93%, the Waltham Cross bypass accounting for most of the unstraight 7%. The Withdrawal Poster It's better than some and less good than others. The map is very complicated because it includes every single bus stop on two routes. It's trying to show that one route is being withdrawn while two other routes are both curtailed and diverted, all on the same map. However the text is about withdrawing just one route and how to cope afterwards. It offers this advice correctly but sub-optimally. Effectively it says "when the 349 disappears use the 279, unless your journey includes Enfield Bus Garage in which case use the 259". What it omits to say is "for any journey inbetween Ponders End and Seven Sisters you can catch either the 259 OR the 279". This is most journeys, but this broad advice has been skipped to focus on edge cases. The playing fields of Harrow School, the spire of St Mary's Church and various villas on the slopes below. However Roxeth isn't the cultured enclave at the top of Harrow Hill it's a suburb at the bottom, originally a village to the southwest , hence arguably Harrow-Under-The Hill. It's another example of somewhere that does have a station, indeed it has two, but ever since the bigger one was called South Harrow in 1903 the original name's been ebbing away. It lingers in streetnames, also the local library, park and two schools, whereas the local authority ward of the same name is a modern invention and doesn't quite match the original Roxeth at all. Let's start on the opposite side of the road to my first photo where we find Roxeth's oldest building, a 17th century weatherboarded farmhouse called Roxeth Farm. Alas the owners have sought to shield their property behind a very high hedge so all you can see is a hipped roof from the side and a sash-windowed slot at the front, but it does look to be delightfully wonky. I had wondered if the barn out back was another rural survivor but no, it's one of three pavilions for Harrow School's extensive cricket fields , the Philathletic Ground. According to the whiteboard on West Street the last matches played here were against Merchant Taylors' on 20th June, over ten weeks ago, because one thing that termly fees of £21,990 deliver is a very long summer break. The centre of the village was a four-way junction on the Northolt Road, now a five-way maelstrom called Roxeth Corner. The only building a Victorian would remember is The Half Moon pub, a half-timbered beauty originally named after the shape of the village pond. Its place in history relates to Britain's first fatal car accident in 1899 which, as a plaque elsewhere attests, took place below Harrow School during a descent of Grove Hill. The Half Moon was merely the site of the subsequent public enquiry, hearing how a rear wheel collapsed and two passengers were hurled from their seats, one dying instantly and the other from his injuries three days later. Perhaps unsurprisingly the pub is now an Indian Grill and Shisha Lounge called the Salt Bar, but if you still want a more traditional local try The White Horse a short walk up Middle Hill. The road rising eastwards here is Roxeth Hill, this the route the 258 bus takes to climb from South Harrow to the upper heights of Harrow School. Full marks to the TfL employee who designated the bus stop halfway up with the letters RH . Roxeth Hill is lined by some of the finer buildings erected as the suburb expanded, from small-scale workers' cottages to Arts and Crafts semis, also rustic Christ Church built to cater to a growing population and set back from the main road. Roxeth Primary still educates pupils in an angular hall built for that very purpose in 1851, indeed it's Harrow's oldest surviving state school. I suspect the triple-bend footbridge shoehorned outside is pupil-related, self-evidently over-engineered when a lollipop lady would do, but the upper span does offer excellent views across the rooftops of Roxeth and the plains of Ruislip. By contrast the main road south from Roxeth Corner is architecturally grim . Here former pubs and cottages have been replaced by dubious postwar and postmillennial flats, while the former petrol station has become a drab stacked hotel. The largest presence is Harrow Police Station (alas not Roxeth Police Station), an outdated flag-flying office block whose front desk remains at risk of closure. Arguably the big Waitrose is a big improvement on what was on the site before, namely a mighty tall gasholder with the letters 'NO' painted on the side, this because it was a key navigational landmark on the approach to Northolt airfield. The sole attractive building on this stretch is the clubhouse of the Royal British Legion's Harrow branch which was built in 1927 in Dutch style, its bar and function room even busier visually than the twiddly exterior . Which brings us to the tube station, namely South Harrow, which was opened in 1903 by the District Railway and transferred to the Piccadilly line in 1932. Charles Holden designed the new station building which outside looks to be less of a stunner than usual, but inside has a whoppingly broad ticket hall and a pair of delightful recessed benches halfway up the stairs in case an ascent of 40 steps proves too much. To the north of the station the railway crosses Roxeth Marsh on a low viaduct , hard though it is today to imagine the adjacent avenues as mushy fields. But just down to the left is the source of the River Roxbourne, a minor brook so named because it rises outside Roxeth, and I've previously blogged that in depth so won't dive in again. More relevant is what's been crammed under the arches immediately opposite the station. This is South Harrow Market , one of London's quirkier retail hideaways, essentially two long alleyways serving a warren of tiny bazaars. Most serve up food, so you may need to push past a delivery driver or two, while others will print you a banner, buy your gold or stab needles in your feet. The curse of AI graphics has struck several of the menus, hence I found the Nepalese and Gujarati pictures less convincing than the proper photos at Syria Food. Again it's a shame it's not called Roxeth Market, given it's right on the edge of the original village, but the nominative pull of the adjacent tube station has proved too strong. Continue down the Northolt Road and barely any businesses mention the old place, with only Roxeth Library flying the flag. Even the Chiltern Railways station at the foot of the hill was only called 'South Harrow and Roxeth' for the first three years after opening, after which it was renamed Northolt Park thanks to the creation of a neighbouring housing estate, thus Roxeth's chances of long-term renown were scuppered. For a proper commemoration best see the information boards at the entrance to Roxeth Recreation Ground, these a step up from Harrow's normal design. The text confirms that the name "Hroecs Seath" was first mentioned in monastic documents in 845AD, even if nobody's 100% sure what Hroecs Seath meant, also that several trees in the park are leftovers from ancient field boundaries. You have alas missed this year's Roxeth Show , the revival of a 1970s tradition, because that was in July. Across the railway line from the rec is South Hill Drive, a lengthy avenue whose streetsign has the unusual combination of a 'No Through Road' symbol and underneath "Except by Toll Road". Follow along and all looks normal at first until suddenly the road forks at two white gates , both closed to vehicles unless you have the correct gizmo to open them. The low road enters land owned by the South Hill Estate while the high road enters the Mount Park Estate, another private residential enclave . Both declare that there is NO THOROUGHFARE FOR THE GENERAL PUBLIC but fail to clarify whether pedestrians are included so I strode through a side gate, greeted a resident walking down the hill with a Waitrose bag and chanced my arm. It feels more Surrey than Middlesex, a sylvan climb where villas and minor mansions still feel the need to hide behind high fences and hedges despite supposedly being private anyway. Some have odd names like The Hut (which definitely isn't) or The Site, while others go for supreme Metro-land bland and call themselves Northmount, Southview, Hillcrest or The Oaks. A dozen have been here since the 19th century, a few are totally-out of character modern flats, and I have no idea how residents successfully held suburbia at bay but it's an extraordinary and privileged residential backwater nonetheless. I exited unscathed through a gate near the top of Sudbury Hill, still historically in ye olde Roxeth, another patch of secret London unlocked. posted 07:00 : Wednesday, September 02, 2026 31 unblogged things I did in August Sat 1: I have never previously tried to get ten days' blogposts prepared in advance whilst also writing posts for current publication. He's so small, also his nails are surprisingly long, also he wriggles a lot, also I'd like to think that was a smile, also thanks for filling your nappy five minutes before we arrived, also by the time he's my age there still won't have been a total solar eclipse in the UK. Sat 29: Christmas puddings, festive bakewells and panettone are back on the shelves in Tesco, and obviously I bought six mince pies to celebrate. Sun 30: Radio 4 Extra repeated an episode of The Grumbleweeds from 1986 (blimey, as late as that?), and I can't believe we found it funny and listened every week. Mon 31: On Instagram I watched reels of people having a great bank holiday abroad, at festivals, up mountains, at restaurants, on rivers, at airports, at weddings etc and all I did was walk across Selsdon Woods and Southwark Bridge. Must try harder. posted 07:00 : Tuesday, September 01, 2026 25 things we learnt from TfL FoI requests in August 2026 1) In the first half of 2026 TfL earned £2,374,283 from 90,511 Penalty Charge Notices for bus lane infringements. 2) The TfL bus fleet comprises 6528 double deckers and 2454 single deckers, of which 2357 are diesel, 2937 electric, 3668 hybrid and 20 hydrogen. 3) The estimated cost of replacing the platform canopies at Barons Court station is £10.3m. 4) The three junctions responsible for the greatest number of yellow box penalty charge notices are i) West Hill/Wandsworth Fire Station SW18, ii) Homerton High St/Homerton Fire Station E9, iii) Vauxhall Bridge Road/Rampayne Street SW1. 5) So far this year, 12% of bus damage incidents have involved a Wrightbus Eclipse Gemini 3, 10% have involved an ADL Enviro 400H MMC and 9% have involved a Wrightbus NRM. 6) With regard to automatic numberplate recognition, TfL operate 4243 enforcement cameras and 181 monitoring cameras. 7) Since fares restarted on bus routes through the Silvertown and Blackwall Tunnel, passenger numbers on route 108 are down 15% compared to the same time period in 2025. On route SL4 numbers are up 4% and on route 129 up 0.5%. 8) Last year in the borough of Greenwich, while crossing the road, 9 pedestrians were seriously injured on a pedestrian crossing, 6 within 50m of a pedestrian crossing and 10 elsewhere. 9) Between February and July on the Northern line, 9% of timetabled trains failed to serve the Battersea extension. 10) The four criteria used to assess tube seats following a deep clean are i) Dust or debris in crevices ii) Dust or debris on seats iii) Grime or dust on panels iv) Gum residue. The required pass mark is 80%. 11) Last year on the Underground there were 5149 reported incidents of passengers possessing an open container of alcohol but only 203 of passengers consuming alcohol. 12) Employee headcount at the eight operational control centres for the tube is 8 for the Waterloo & City, 48 for the Bakerloo, 50 for the Victoria, 65 for the Central, 69 for the Piccadilly, 76 for the Northern, 92 for the Jubilee and 247 for the combined Circle, District, Hammersmith & City and Metropolitan. 13) The new signage on the bus lane on Westminster Bridge Road incorrectly omitted motorcycles from the list of permitted vehicles so has been removed pending replacement. 14) In the last year the drivers of 63 TfL maintenance vans have been caught exceeding a 20mph speed limit. 15) Since the start of last year the tube line with the greatest number of reported robberies was the Central line, while theft of public property was most prevalent on the Piccadilly line. The Northern line was top for violence, sexual offences and public disorder. 16) If you'd like a copy of all the in-carriage line diagrams used on the tube, DLR and trams, here's a zip folder . 17) TfL's total expenditure on taxi services during the 2025/26 financial year was £6,968,396. 18) In the last financial year 3,335,464 passengers on 190,439 buses were checked by revenue staff, leading to 17,947 penalty fares being issued and 2892 successful prosecutions. 19) Over the last three months 25% of Elizabeth line services at Acton Main Line departed at least three minutes late. 20) In the week starting 29th June a bus on route 70 knocked a motorcyclist off his bike in South Kensington and another bus on route 70 crashed into a house in Notting Hill. The same driver was not responsible for both incidents. 21) There are no current plans to introduce any new weekend-only Night Services on the tube, Overground or buses. 22) When planning for a possible Rotherhithe to Canary Wharf footbridge, a report estimated that a 15m high bridge would require opening 1-4 times an hour in the navigational peak, whereas a 20m bridge would have 95% availability. 23) 43,641 London addresses are registered to two active 60+ Oyster photocards, 864 hold three and 116 hold more than three. 24) In the last twelve months the vehicle with the highest number of ULEZ Penalty Charge Notices is a Ford Focus Titanium X TDCi with 361 fines. The vehicle with the highest number of Congestion Charge PCNs has a diplomatic plate (290 fines). 25) If you ask TfL to use their office printer to print out every tube map ever produced in colour on A3 paper, along with guidance on how to fold them, they will refuse. posted 08:00 : Belated transport news I missed reporting on several transport stories while I was away so here's a brief catch-up. 🚦 This Saturday the gyratory at St Paul's is being tweaked . The southern end of King Edward Street is being pedestrianised (to create Greyfriars Square) so traffic will have to go a different way and so will local buses. Precisely where the 4, 8, 25, 56, 76 and 133 stop will be altering, and route 100 has already been extended to St Bart's. TfL have produced a ridiculously complicated map to try to explain things (my head exploded), so if you need to catch a bus the City of London's vastly oversimplified version should be clearer. 🚡 It amazes me that every time I do one of these round-ups there's a new thing at the cablecar but there always is. This time it's an interactive audio guide you can listen to on the way across with different stories in either direction. It's narrated by Engi-Bear, the cablecar's lumpen mascot, and produced by an Italian software team called POPGuide . You need to bring your own headphones (and indeed your own phone). The unusual thing is that it costs £1, just £1, when they could have given it away for free or tried to make more money out of it. Upselling has never been so flaccid. 🚇 TfL have added another weekday closure of most of the Piccadilly line to their already excessive roster of downtime, specifically Wednesday 28th - Friday 30th October (immediately before a full line closure at the weekend). Whatever is wrong with the new trains must be proving intractable, given it'll be at least next spring before any member of the public gets on board, fingers crossed. 🚌 London's next dead bus is the 349 which is being withdrawn on Saturday. Expect bloggage. On the same day the latest Superloop route is being introduced, the SL12 from Gants Hill to Rainham. The good news that it'll be free to use for the first week, should you happen to live in the area. TfL have produced a route diagram and a long list of stops in both directions, but not a map because that would be too useful. I cannot overemphasise enough how remote the Rainham terminus is, so expect bloggage there too. 📽️ In mid-August TfL published their Advertising Annual Report , a glossy 49 page compilation of all the showiest campaigns of the last year. It reads like a bunch of talented professionals congratulating themselves on a job well done, but unfortunately that job is to make their advertising more and more difficult to miss. Key phrases include "empowering brands to unlock creativity and turn heads" and "innovation remains central to our shared focus". The scariest project is a "plan to deliver world-first, ten-metre-long digital corridor wraps in selected Elizabeth line stations", i.e. huge moving screens you can't take your eyes off. It's so controversial they've made a full-scale mock-up at UCL "to evaluate how digital corridor wraps might impact the experience of customers who are neurodivergent or disabled". See photo. They hope the research will show any potential impacts can be mitigated, but I hope someone will grow a conscience and halt the introduction of these massive digital intrusions. Advertising targets shouldn't be fixated on increasing distraction, forever designing formats it's more and more impossible to take our eyes off. 📱 The report also suggests you could be seeing a lot more adverts on TfL Go in future. At present the app generates 76 million page views a month but only made £5,000 in revenue last year, thus "TfL Go represents a significant long-term growth opportunity". 🚌 If you enjoy those free heritage bus days when the London Bus Museum floods a historic route with vintage vehicles, the list of planned events has extended. Route 85: 2nd October 2027. posted 07:00 : Monday, August 31, 2026 THE BASQUE COUNTRY Bilbao & its transport [70 photos] San Sebastián & cideria [50 photos] Biarritz France [40 photos] VITORIA- GASTEIZ & total solar eclipse [60 photos] DLR trains salt valley La Rioja [←40 photos→] Pamplona posted 09:00 : This blog loves a boundary and the border between Spain and France is one of the more significant. It's 425 miles long, was finally settled in 1856 and mostly follows the drainage divide of the Pyrenees. At its western end it divides the towns of Irun (Spain) and Hendaye (France), or more precisely the Spanish town of Hondarribia and the French suburb of Zokuburu. If you stand in Hondarribia's main square and look down the hill you can see where the border ends at the mouth of the river Bidasoa . Spain's on the left, France on the right. There are many ways to cross the border here. By road European route E5 crosses the border four miles upstream at the Zubi Nazioartekoa . On the Spanish side the autoroute is designated AP-8 , then morphs into the A63 to Bordeaux in the middle of the bridge. The French side immediately welcomes drivers with a toll booth, or if viewed the other way charges drivers for leaving the country. There are no passport checks or customs, nor at the two non-motorway bridges between the two sides. We returned via the more minor Santiago Bridge, freely crossing thanks to EU accords which have made the former queues obsolete. That said we did pass French gendarmes setting up beside the road ready to spot-check inbound traffic, so maybe be careful what you choose to take in or out. By rail A 120m-long railway bridge links Spanish railways to France, which is awkward because the countries have very different gauges. There are thus a heck of a lot of marshalling yards on either side to aid transfer of rolling stock. A parallel bridge carries the Euskotren metro train from San Sebastián but this travels only 400m into France before terminating at Hendaye station. Long distance rail travellers need to transfer to the Euskotren to make their connection, or else lug their luggage for a mile and a half via the Santiago Bridge. We had hoped to visit Biarritz by train but the connecting faff (and oddly infrequent services on the French side) made it far better to drive instead. [The Man in Seat 61] By boat The lowest crossing of the border is the ferry that's been shuttling between Hondarribia and Hendaye since 1993. The service crosses Txingudi Bay in seven minutes flat for the ferry reasonable fare of €2.50. The jetty was only a ten minute walk from where I took today's first photo so I was sorely tempted to make a pointless border crossing just for the sake of it. My travelling companions instead prioritised lunch so we settled at Mika Jatetxea for pintxos and pork rib with orange and cheddar sauce and I missed my chance. Also best not risk a trip to a foreign country when your plane leaves in three hours, so Hondarribia's lovely walled town was a far safer bet. By air For reasons of flatness San Sebastián's airport is 10 miles east of the city in Hondarribia, built on reclaimed land in the Bidasoa estuary. For reasons of space the runway is short so gets only a handful of flights daily, all in small planes including a few weekly returns to London City Airport. For reasons of geography the runway is incredibly close to the mid-stream national border, the centre of the runway barely 100m away, indeed only a few seconds after take-off you've already entered French airspace. If you remember the very first photo I showed you at the start of my holiday travelogue , taken from the window of my departing plane, that had Spain in the foreground, France in the background and the Santiago Bridge inbetween. One holiday, two countries, and somehow it's taken me longer to write up than I spent there. posted 08:00 : If you've driven all the way to France you might as well stop somewhere else on the way back. ✉ A postcard from Saint-Jean-de-Luz On my summer holidays we went to Saint-Jean-de-Luz which is in France but only just. It is six miles from Spain on the coast and it has a big bay and ice creams. It is not a fun place to park but we managed. The place to go is the beach , it is long and very sandy. A lot of people were playing beach volleyball because there is a lot of space . The sun was starting to set over the fort and lighthouse at the far end of the bay and it was very pretty . But nobody was in the sea because the purple flag was flying. The purple flag means JELLYFISH! or in this case Portuguese men o' war because they had invaded . I have never seen a purple flag before it is serious, if one stings you in precisely the wrong place you could die. The lifeguards sounded a big horn when they saw someone wading in. It must be gutting if you come here for a week's holiday and a blue bag of venom stops you going in the water. The biggest building on the promenade is the casino , there is always a casino although this one closed a while back. It has a boardwalk and a pergola and little shops. We bought ice creams from a Glaces Lopez van on the promenade, they've been going since 1924. I had citron in a cornet, it was yummy and only €1.70 which is a total bargain. We also bought Gâteaux Basques from Maison Adam in the high street but only the small ones, I liked the custard filling best. Maison Adam are most famous for their macarons , they once made them for the wedding of Louis XIV and Marie Theresa of Spain which took place here in Saint-Jean-de-Luz in 1660. Now that's an origin story! The high street is proper characterful, all narrow with brightly-painted shutters. It's also a bit designer in places, such is the tourist clientele, although if you buy surf gear you have to go out of town to use it because the bay doesn't get big waves. At the lower end are a lot of outdoor bar tables, London has nothing on this, also the marina where the nice boats are. The smart dockfront museum is the House of the Infanta , this because Marie Theresa spent the night before her wedding here ( Maison Louis XIV is just round the corner). The harbour is also the mouth of the Nivelle but it is not a famous river. On the way back to the car we passed the public fronton , which is the place where they play pelote . I first learned about pelote in my Tricolore textbook and now here I was watching two Basque lads hurling a ball really hard against a wall using their long curved xistera. Then they had to stop playing because a truck arrived with tree trunks for tonight's Basque Strength event , a display of athletic sawing, bale lifting, sack racing and tug of war. We didn't have time to stay but what with the pelote, games and gâteaux we had learned that Saint-Jean-de-Luz is just as Basque as towns the other side of the Spanish border. text: We feel abandoned by police in crimewave, say Kings Heath residents Skip to content Watch Live Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live 'We feel abandoned by police': A community's despair after months of crime 15 hours ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Rebecca Woods & Eleanor Lawson in Kings Heath BBC More than 100 incidents have been linked to the same group, MP Al Carns says Working on a busy high street, staff at Subway in Kings Heath, Birmingham, are used to dealing with tricky customers. Teenagers leaping over the counter to steal entire trays of crisps and cookies, however, is not something they were prepared for. The fizzy drinks fridge has been ransacked numerous times over the summer, the front door and windows smashed. Customers who were unfortunate to witness the attacks have been verbally abused, with one also having his bike vandalised. "We've had a number of staff leave recently," one worker says. "They should not have to come to work in fear." Along the road at Greggs, the gang has rushed in to steal armfuls of food. On one occasion, a female worker who tried to lock the doors to stop them was assaulted by a teenage girl. A convenience store has been targeted so often they have to keep the doors locked all evening, the manager says as he scrolls through CCTV images of thefts and vandalism. At Coustis hair salon, where hairdressing siblings Tina Bartlam and Antonio Constantinou have been for 40 years, the windows are boarded up after being smashed. Kings Heath is known for its good schools, independent shops, lively music and art scene and strong community spirit. But in recent months, the actions of a few have caused many to feel unsafe and unsure of who is in control. A female shopworker was assaulted by a teenage girl among a gang stealing food Community groups on Facebook are filled with eyewitness reports of crimes taking place almost daily, fuelling anger and questions about why no-one seems to be able to put to a stop to it. Insp Hayley Thompson, who oversees policing in Kings Heath, said the force took anti-social behaviour "incredibly seriously" and they were working to make the area safer. But Matt Powell from Enjoy Kings Heath, the area's Business Improvement District (BID), who has been taking calls from distressed shop owners for months, is sceptical. "This community has been let down by the police," he says. "People feel like they've been abandoned." He has had a good relationship with officers over the years, but feels the lack of reassurance to the public about the recent crimewave has created a "vacuum" for people to consider vigilantism. Traders in Kings Heath are very worried about the rise in crime, says Matt Powell An even bigger problem, he says, is drug dealing taking place openly in the streets. Shoplifting is another major issue. Powell says he understands the pressures of modern day policing and assumes something is happening behind the scenes they may not be privy to. But "the lack of visible policing is surely making people feel like they can get away with it", he says. In July, West Midlands Police and Crime Commissioner (PCC), Labour's Simon Foster, said £12.2m funding had paid for 150 new police officers in neighbourhood teams along with 20 police community support officers (PCSOs). Another 139 officers are being redeployed into local teams to focus on a "prevention and problem solving approach". Talking to people on the high street, they feel it was a mistake to shut Kings Heath police station. It closed for good in 2025, 10 years after its front desk stopped taking inquiries from the public. Officers from the neighbourhood policing team are based just over a mile away at Moseley Police Station, but there are concerns Kings Heath falls down the list of priorities. Kings Heath park is popular with families but there have been numerous reports of anti-social behaviour over summer Others waiting to speak to police are the parents of four boys who were threatened with a knife at Kings Heath Park. The boys, aged 11 to 14, had gone there in the early evening of 29 August while their parents were at a function in the Red Lion pub. They were approached by three teenagers and a scuffle ensued. A youth brandished a knife and told one of the visiting boys to "get on your knees", which, terrified, he did. "They managed to escape - my brother ran and knocked on the door of the nearest house but no-one was in so they ran back to the pub," the boy's older sister says. Her 11-year-old son and his friend had run away in fear but found a couple walking their dog who returned them safely to their parents. While they spoke with police on the night, the family says no searches or arrests were made in the area, and a week after the ordeal they have still not been contacted by officers. The force told the BBC it was unable to comment on this case. Policing at 'breaking point' Recently installed Lime scooters and bikes near the new Kings Heath railway station have been spotted being used by children as young as 12, who are dangerously weaving in and out of traffic and kicking cars. The bikes should only be ridden by over 18s and identification is required for anyone setting up an account. Lime says it is working with police to help prevent underage riding and wants members of the public to report incidents to it. It also urges adults not to unlock vehicles for children, adding it is a "shared responsibility". Councillor Hamzah Sheikh says he is extremely concerned people do not feel safe The crimewave led Councillor Jordan Phillip to write a public letter to West Midlands Police asking for a meeting to discuss the force's plan of action. "There is a growing perception among residents that the problem remains unaddressed and the situation is continuing unchecked," he wrote. His Green Party colleague, Councillor Hamzah Sheikh, is the lead on anti-social behaviour for the ward and also sits on the West Midlands Police and Crime Panel. "I've lived here for three years," he said. "It has changed to the point that people don't feel safe walking up the high street." When asked if the area had been let down by police, he nodded. "Neighbourhood policing is at breaking point," he says. "They have a hard job and they don't have the resources to do what they've got to do." A woman who was assaulted near the railway station says police have kept her informed during their investigation. Two shop owners say they have been visited by officers but agree much more needs to be done. Kings Heath police station closed in 2025 Sheikh says he has spoken to the parents of some of the youths accused of running riot. One mother has received death threats, possibly triggered by anger on social media. "The mother is distraught. She's doing everything she can," he says of the struggle to control her child's actions. Many people are sympathetic and want to help. A number of residents say a multi-agency approach is needed - that it is not just about the police, but also education, structure and support from social services and the community. Cleveland police chief proud of force but being 'let down' by funding 'I'd rather die than ring the police': Distrust and fear in Middlesbrough after A66 crash Al Carns, the MP for Birmingham Selly Oak which includes part of Kings Heath, says he is well aware of problems, with more than 100 offences thought to have been committed by the same group. "It started as petty anti-social behaviour pre-Christmas and has escalated to significant shoplifting and theft. We've got to put an end to it," he says. He says neighbourhood officers have increased by 49% in a year, which is significant, and urges people to get in touch with him if they continue to have issues. On Sunday, police confirmed three teenage boys had been charged in connection with some of the issues. A 13-year-old faces charges including possession of a weapon, criminal damage, assault and theft of motor vehicle. Another 13-year-old and a boy of 14 have been charged with theft of a motor vehicle. All three are due to appear in court at a later date. In a newly-released statement , the force said seven weapons had been seized and seven people had been arrested for possession of a knife and offensive weapons, assault and possessing drugs with intent to supply. An investigation into reports of youths threatening children with a machete is also ongoing. "We want everyone to enjoy living or visiting Kings Heath and not be intimidated," Insp Thompson says. Kings Heath has a thriving arts and music scene and a monthly farmers' market The PCC says the "serious concerns raised have been immediately escalated to the Chief Superintendent of Birmingham Local Policing Area". "I expect the local Neighbourhood Team to tackle the crime and anti-social behaviour as a matter of urgency," he added. He said West Midlands Police had 500 fewer police officers and 500 fewer PCSOs than in 2010 but "the majority of other police force areas have more than they have ever had". "I have been repeatedly calling on government to ensure our region receives its fair share of officers and funding for over five years, but unfortunately government will not listen and will not act," he said. A Home Office spokeswoman says it is delivering "the biggest reforms to policing in over 200 years to allow forces to focus on protecting their community". "Police force funding this year is at a historic high of £18.5bn, with West Midlands Police seeing a cash increase of 4.1%." A wider review of the police funding formula will also take place to ensure it is "fair and responsive to local needs", a statement added. 'This is redeemable' The feeling of lawlessness has galvanised the community in many ways. A petition has been started urging authorities to work together to protect residents. The councillors say they are committed to helping to turn things around. "I'm fighting for this community. I want to be here for the rest of my life," Sheikh tells the BBC. Coustis's Tina Bartlam says they have been feeling "abandoned and vulnerable" but that swift, hard work is needed to recover. "This is redeemable, but it needs to be done quickly," she says. "We need a short, sharp shock." Follow BBC Birmingham on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . title: Turn Firefox into a screen reader with Fire Vox | 456 Berea Street
description: Fire Vox is a free, open source, cross platform screen reader extension for Firefox. If you create websites you need it.
headings: Turn Firefox into a screen reader with Fire Vox
text: Turn Firefox into a screen reader with Fire Vox | 456 Berea Street Skip to main content About Archive Lab Turn Firefox into a screen reader with Fire Vox Iâve sen Fire Vox mentioned plenty of times but have never had any luck getting it to work on my Mac. Until now, that is. Not sure what Iâve been doing wrong the other times I have tried it, but the other day I gave it another shot and it worked without any problems. For anyone who hasnât heard of Fire Vox, it is a free, open source screen reader extension for Firefox that works on Windows, Mac OS X, and Linux. Among other things it has support for WAI-ARIA and the CSS3 Speech Module , and is a good alternative to VoiceOver if youâre on a Mac and need a screen reader for web browsing (or testing). One thing that had me a little bit confused at first is that, at least as far as I can tell, you need to tab into a freshly loaded page before the âAuto Readâ option ( Ctrl + Shift + a ) will work. Read Next ( Ctrl + Shift + f ) and Read Previous ( Ctrl + Shift + d ) work even if the focus is still in the location bar. Not sure if that is intentional or not, but if you load up a site and nothing happens when you press Ctrl + Shift + a to have Fire Vox read the entire page, try using tab or ( Ctrl + Shift + f ) to move keyboard focus to the loaded page first. For developers Fire Vox makes it easy to check how their sites work in a screen reader. Sure, itâs just one of several available screen readers, but this one is free and cross-platform. In other words there is no reason for you not to have it installed, so grab a copy right now. Balemoyi abdigaldaki tiyid : Muyquytá Zipazgo cosxo is Hunza Zacazgo cosxo is Iraca tumtaxo is Tundama tumtaxo voxis konako mivvexaxo. Xanta Mali lekeugal, Muisca va yerumara wali staba ksubeyed numen sina kadayad vangluyara ke yona doda. Ison vuwafa waldura gu vindara wal amidafa doda iku banafa fiste zo divatceyer, isen dofa vegedusa lagara dum lavakiraf bolk ta midura va ontinafa taya, isen sayakafa tanara ta likera va volnafa mikra dum Panche is Muzo, va lomantafa vangluyara tuadrayar. Bata kotcoba di tiyir tazukafa riga ke abdigalda. Lopof andik ta ardil is targuca is gaderopafi is skapafi roti va sint likeyed ise va sintafa doda lalevbenpluyud. Bata koboda va geja daskiyid. Voxen cenen okilik va gadera va staba is doda me mbi deswayad nume grustara ke dodeem is stabeem zo nendoyeyed. Opelon cenesik va intafa ardilafa tirka laumasiyir numaze va vamoefa gorara ronovaskiyir ise va kiewega loote mbi kserayar. Zipazgo cosxo moni 1450 awiyir, gadenon gan Saguamachica gejayasa va Panche mikra, aze kali 1541 lapteyer viele espanafa olgalicura va istexo ke refa Kolombia ceneson tenukeyer. Muisca balumaks va lan mepilkomodan Zipa nafalik, re viden dene Tcila ke Moava koe Bogotá. Cosxo ke Muisca abdigalda va kipi ke ontinafa gola ke Ronefa Rodega koe Kolombia modivatceyer, koe refa Cundinamarca winka isu Boyacá isu Santander . Koe Cundinamarca, xopo tiyid azekexa ke Bogotá is Ubaté is Pacho krant isu Fusagasugá isu Tenza isu Cáqueza ; koe Boyacá : Tunja is Moniquirá is Chiquinquirá is Duitama is Villa de Leyva is Sogamoso ; vagee Santander : wale Suárez kuksa isu Chicamocha . Grustara Muisca abdigalda vas cosxo vas mon 47 000 km² ruldayar, valentu Chicamocha gola vage Páramo de Sumapaz gee Bogotá, is vataltu Vélez is Zipacón varon datca ke Ronefa Rodega tite azeka ke Meta golapa. Sanelia ke cosxo tiyir vas mon 1200000 irubasik ba artlakira ke espanik. title: ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ
headings: ನಿಮಗೆ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಅಥವಾ ವಿಕಿ ಬಳಗದ ಇತರ ಯೋಜನೆಗಳು ಉಪಯೋಗಕ್ಕೆ ಬಂದಲ್ಲಿ, ಈ ಪುಟಗಳನ್ನು ಆತಿಥೇಯವಹಿಸಿರುವ ವಿಕಿಮೀಡಿಯ ಫೌಂಡೇಶನ್‌ಗೆ ದೇಣಿಗೆ ನೀಡಬಹುದು. ದಯವಿಟ್ಟು ದೇಣಿಗೆ ನೀಡಲು ಈ ಪುಟಕ್ಕೆ ಭೇಟಿ ನೀಡಿ (ದೇಣಿಗೆ ಲಿಂಕ್ ವಿಕಿಮೀಡಿಯ ಫೌಂಡೇಶನ್‌ಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ & ಜಾಲತಾಣ ಆಂಗ್ಲ ಭಾಷೆಯಲ್ಲಿದೆ).
text: ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ವಿಷಯಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಗು ಪಟ್ಟಿ ಪಟ್ಟಿ move to sidebar ಮರೆ ಮಾಡಿ ಸಂಚರಣೆ ಮುಖ್ಯ ಪುಟ ಸಮುದಾಯ ಪುಟ ಪ್ರಚಲಿತ ಇತ್ತೀಚೆಗಿನ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳು ಯಾವುದೋ ಒಂದು ಪುಟ ಸಹಾಯ ಅರಳಿ ಕಟ್ಟೆ ವಿಶೇಷ ಪುಟಗಳು ಹುಡುಕು ಹುಡುಕು ಗೋಚರ ದೇಣಿಗೆ ಹೊಸ ಮೂಲವನ್ನು ನೋಡು ಇತಿಹಾಸವನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಇಲ್ಲಿಗೆ ಯಾವ ಸಂಪರ್ಕ ಕೂಡುತ್ತದೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಪಟ್ಟ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳು ಸ್ಥಿರ ಕೊಂಡಿ ಪುಟದ ಮಾಹಿತಿ ಈ ಪುಟವನ್ನು ಉಲ್ಲೇಖಿಸಿ ಪುಟ್ಟ ಕೊಂಡಿ Switch to legacy parser ಮುದ್ರಿಸು/ರಫ್ತು ಮಾಡು ವಿಕಿಸ್ಪಿಶೀಸ್ ವಿಕಿಡಾಟ Wikifunctions ವಿಕಿಮೇನಿಯಾ ವಿಕಿಕೋಟ್ ವಿಕಿಸೋರ್ಸ್ ವಿಕ್ಷನರಿ ವಿಕಿಡಾಟಾ ವಸ್ತು ಗೋಚರ move to sidebar ಮರೆ ಮಾಡಿ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯದಿಂದ, ಇದು ಮುಕ್ತ ಹಾಗೂ ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯಕ್ಕೆ ಸ್ವಾಗತ ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಕನ್ನಡದ ಒಂದು ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ಈ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶ ಬಹು ಭಾಷೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಲಭ್ಯವಿದೆ. ಪ್ರಸ್ತುತ ಕನ್ನಡ ಆವೃತ್ತಿಯು ೩೫,೬೭೧ ವಿಷಯಗಳ ಕುರಿತಾದ ಪುಟಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿದೆ. ಅನುವಾದಿಸಲು, ಸಂಪಾದಕರಾಗಲು ಉತ್ಸಾಹವಿರುವವರು ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯದ ಸಮುದಾಯ ಪುಟಕ್ಕೆ ಭೇಟಿ ನೀಡಿ . ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಬರೆಯುವುದರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಸಹಾಯಕ್ಕಾಗಿ ಲಿಪ್ಯಂತರ ಸಹಾಯ ಪುಟವನ್ನು , ಕೀಲಿಮಣೆ ಅಪ್ಲಿಕೇಶನ್ , ಇನ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಪರಿಕರವನ್ನು ನೋಡಿ. ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಪಾದನೆ ಕಲಿಯಲು ಪ್ರಯೋಗಾರ್ಥ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಪುಟವನ್ನು ಉಪಯೋಗಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳಬಹುದು. ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯ ಕುರಿತು ಒಂದು ಅಂಚೆಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆ ಕೂಡ ಇದೆ , ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಸಹಾಯ ಪಡೆಯಲು ಅಂಚೆಪೆಟ್ಟಿಗೆಗೆ ನೋಂದಾಯಿಸಿಕೊಂಡು wikikn-l@lists.wikimedia.org ವಿಳಾಸಕ್ಕೆ ಇ-ಮೇಲ್ ಕಳುಹಿಸಬಹುದು. ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯದ ಐ.ಆರ್.ಸಿ # wikimedia-kn ಸಂಪರ್ಕ ಸಾಧಿಸಿ ಚಾನಲ್ ಮುಖಾಂತರ ಸಂಪರ್ಕ ಸಾಧಿಸಬಹುದು. ವಿಶೇಷ ಸೂಚನೆ: ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಕಿಪೀಡಿಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಕನ್ನಡ ಲಿಪಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತ್ರ ಬರೆಯಿರಿ. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಕೇಳಲಾಗುವ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು (FAQ) ವಿಶೇಷ ಲೇಖನ ಕನ್ನಡ ಅಕ್ಷರಮಾಲೆ 'ಅ' ಕನ್ನಡ ಅಕ್ಷರಮಾಲೆಯು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಿ ಲಿಪಿಯಿಂದ ಬೆಳೆದು ಬಂದಿದೆ. ಇದನ್ನು ಸ್ವರಗಳು, ಅನುಸ್ವಾರ, ವಿಸರ್ಗ, ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳು, ಅವರ್ಗೀಯ ವ್ಯಂಜನಗಳೆಂದು ವಿಭಾಗಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ. ಕನ್ನಡ ಅಕ್ಷರಮಾಲೆಯನ್ನು ಕನ್ನಡ ವರ್ಣಮಾಲೆಯೆಂದು ಕರೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ನಾವು ಮಾತನಾಡುವ ಮಾತುಗಳೆಲ್ಲ ವಾಕ್ಯ ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳಾಗಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ವಾಕ್ಯಗಳು ಪದಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ಪದಗಳು ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳಿಂದ ಕೂಡಿರುತ್ತವೆ. ಉದಾಹರಣೆಗೆ, ನಾನು ಶಾಲೆಗೆ ಹೋಗಿ ಬರುವೆನು. ಈ ವಾಕ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಾನು, ಶಾಲೆಗೆ, ಹೋಗಿ, ಬರುವೆನು, ಹೀಗೆ ನಾಲ್ಕು ಪದಗಳಿವೆ. ಒಂದೊಂದು ಪದದಲ್ಲೂ ಹಲವು ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳಿವೆ. ನಾನು ಎಂಬ ಪದದಲ್ಲಿ ನ್+ಆ+ನ್+ಉ ಎಂಬ ಧ್ವನಿಮಾ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಯ ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳಿವೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಕನ್ನಡ ಭಾಷೆಯನ್ನು ಮಾತನಾಡುವಾಗ ಬಳಸುವ ಅಕ್ಷರಗಳ ಮಾಲೆಗೆ ವರ್ಣಮಾಲೆ ಅಥವಾ ಅಕ್ಷರಮಾಲೆ ಎಂದು ಕರೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. ನಮ್ಮ ಹೊಸ ಲೇಖನಗಳಿಂದ... ಕನ್ನಡ ವಿಶ್ವಕೋಶದ ಸದಸ್ಯರಿಂದ ರಚಿಸಲ್ಪಟ್ಟ ಹೊಸ ಲೇಖನಗಳಿಂದ ಕೆಲವು ಸ್ವಾರಸ್ಯಕರ ಸಂಗತಿಗಳು: ಸುಂಡೋಕು ಎಂದರೆ ಓದಲು ಉದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿ ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳು ಅಥವಾ ಇತರೆ ಓದುವ ಸಾಮಗ್ರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಖರೀದಿಸಿ, ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಓದದೆ ಮನೆಯಲ್ಲೇ ರಾಶಿಯಾಗಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುವ ಪ್ರವೃತ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ಸೂಚಿಸುವ ಜಪಾನೀಸ್ ಪದವಾಗಿದೆ. ಮುಂದೆ ಓದಬೇಕೆಂಬ ಉದ್ದೇಶದಿಂದ ಪುಸ್ತಕದ ಕಪಾಟಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಇಟ್ಟುಕೊಂಡಿರುವ ಆದರೆ ಇನ್ನೂ ಓದದ ಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳನ್ನೂ ಈ ಪದದಿಂದ ಸೂಚಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಬಿ.ಆರ್.ಮಾಣಿಕ್ಯಮ್ (1909–1964) ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಮೊದಲ ನಗರ ಯೋಜನಾ ನಿರ್ದೇಶಕ ರಾಗಿ, ರಾಜ್ಯದ ಮೂಲಸೌಕರ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಪಾತ್ರ ವಹಿಸಿದರು. ಅವರ ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಪ್ರಸಿದ್ಧ ಸಾಧನೆಯೆಂದರೆ ಕರ್ನಾಟಕದ ಶಾಸಕಾಂಗ ಭವನವಾದ ಭವ್ಯವಾದ ವಿಧಾನಸೌಧದ ವಿನ್ಯಾಸ . ವಂಶವೃಕ್ಷ_(ಕಾದಂಬರಿ) ೧೯೬೫ರಲ್ಲಿ ಬಿಡುಗಡೆಯಾದ ಡಾ. ಎಸ್‌.ಎಲ್. ಭೈರಪ್ಪನವರ ಕನ್ನಡ ಕಾದಂಬರಿ. ಸಮಾಜದ ಕಟ್ಟು ಪಾಡನ್ನು ಮುರಿದು ಹೊಸ ಜೀವನಕ್ಕೆ ನಾಂದಿ ಹಾಡುವ ಸಶಕ್ತ ಪಾತ್ರಗಳಿಂದ, ಖ್ಯಾತಿ ಪಡೆದ ಕೃತಿ. ಕಪ್ಪು ಶಿಲೀಂಧ್ರ ಮ್ಯೂಕೋರ್ಮೈಕೋಸಿಸ್ (ಕಪ್ಪು ಶಿಲೀಂದ್ರ) ಎನ್ನುವುದು ಶಿಲೀಂದ್ರಗಳಿಂದ ಉಂಟಾಗುವ ಸೋಂಕು. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಮಣ್ಣು, ಹಳೆಯ ಕಟ್ಟಡಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಒದ್ದೆಯಾದ ಗೋಡೆಗಳು ಇತ್ಯಾದಿಗಳಿಂದ ಈ ಸೋಂಕು ಹರಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಅಭಿನಂದನ್ ವರ್ಧಮಾನ್ ೨೦೧೯ರ ಫೆಬ್ರವರಿ ೨೬ರಂದು ಭಾರತೀಯ ವಾಯುಸೇನೆಯು ಬಾಲಕೋಟ್ ಭಯೋತ್ಪಾದಕ ಶಿಬಿರದ ಮೇಲೆ ನಡೆಸಿದ ವಾಯುದಾಳಿಗೆ ಪ್ರತಿಯಾಗಿ, ಭಾರತೀಯ ಸೇನಾನೆಲೆಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಪಾಕಿಸ್ತಾನದ ವಾಯುಸೇನೆಯು ೨೭ ನೇ ಫೆಬ್ರವರಿ ೨೦೧೯ರಂದು ವಿಫಲ ದಾಳಿಯನ್ನು ನಡೆಸಿದ ಸಂದರ್ಭದಲ್ಲಿ, ಪಾಕ್ ಯುದ್ಧವಿಮಾನವನ್ನು ಅಟ್ಟಿಸಿಕೊಂಡು ಹೋಗಿ, ಪಾಕಿ ವಾಯುಸೇನೆಯ, ಅಮೇರಿಕಾ ನಿರ್ಮಿತ ಎಫ್- ೧೬ ವಿಮಾನವನ್ನು, ಮಿಗ್-೨೧ ಬೈಸನ್ ವಿಮಾನದ ಸಹಾಯದಿಂದ ಹೊಡೆದುರುಳಿಸಿದ ಸಾಹಸಿ ಸೈನಿಕ. ಸಂಪಾದಿಸಿ ಸುದ್ದಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ ೨೧ : ಹೆಸರಾಂತ ನಟಿ ಸಾಹುಕಾರ್ ಜಾನಕಿ (ಚಿತ್ರಿತ) ವಿಧಿವಶ ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ ೨೧ : ಲಡಾಖ್ ‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಜಮ್ಮು ಮತ್ತು ಕಾಶ್ಮೀರ ಹೈಕೋರ್ಟ್‌ ನ ಪೀಠ ಸ್ಥಾಪನೆ ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ ೨೦ : ಬಾಂಗ್ಲಾದೇಶ ದ ನೂತನ ಅಧ್ಯಕ್ಷರಾಗಿ ಆಡಳಿತಾರೂಢ ಬಾಂಗ್ಲಾದೇಶ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯವಾದಿ ಪಕ್ಷದ (ಬಿಎನ್‌ಪಿ) ಅಭ್ಯರ್ಥಿ ಮಿರ್ಜಾ ಫಕ್ರುಲ್ ಇಸ್ಲಾಂ ಅಲಂಗೀರ್ ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ ೨೦ : ನೀಟ್ ಪ್ರತಿಭಟನೆ-ಪೊಲೀಸ್ ದೌರ್ಜನ್ಯ, ತನಿಖೆಗೆ ಉನ್ನತ ಮಟ್ಟದ ಸಮಿತಿ ರಚಿಸಿದ ಸುಪ್ರೀಂಕೋರ್ಟ್ ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ ೨೦ : ಮಧ್ಯ ಆಫ್ರಿಕಾ ದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಿನ್ನದ ಗಣಿ ಕುಸಿದು ೧೦೦ಕ್ಕೂ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಮಂದಿ Dieses Portal soll den Einstieg in die Artikel rund um die Region Oltenien erleichtern. Die Kleine Walachei (dt. auch Oltenien , rum. Oltenia ) ist eine historische Landschaft in Rumänien und ein Teil der Walachei . Sie wird „Kleine Walachei“ genannt, weil sie im Gegensatz zu der Großen Walachei deutlich kleiner ist. Aus der Zeit der ungarischen Herrschaft (etwa 1090–1330) ist auch die Bezeichnung „ Banat von Severin “ überliefert. Zwischen 1718 und 1739 gehörte sie zum Habsburgischen Reich. Gelegentlich wurde die Kleine Walachei als „Banat von Krajowa “, „Valachia Cia-Alutana“ oder „Valachia Caesarea“ benannt. … lese weiter Fehlende Artikel: Radu cel Mare - Radu Negru - Alexandru I. - Bălteni (Ilfov) - Dan II. - Kloster Cozia - Partidul Poporului – Dan Diaconescu - Parâng-Gebirge - Radu I. - Teiș (Dâmbovița) - Vladislav II. (Walachei) Der Jiu ist ein linker Nebenfluss der Donau im Süden Rumäniens . Der Fluss entsteht nahe Petroșani aus dem Jiul de Vest (dt. Westlicher Schil ) und dem Jiul de Est (dt. Östlicher Schil ). Geografie und Natur Die Region umfasst folgende Kreise: Dolj mit den Städten Craiova , Băilești , Calafat , Filiași , Dăbuleni , Poiana Mare , Segarcea , Moțăței , Podari , Dăneți und Călărași . ... siehe weitere Gorj mit den Städten Târgu Jiu , Motru , Rovinari , Bumbești-Jiu , Târgu Cărbunești , Turceni , Tismana und Novaci . ... siehe weitere Mehedinți mit den Städten Drobeta Turnu Severin , Orșova , Strehaia , Vânju Mare und Baia de Aramă . ... siehe weitere Vâlcea mit den Städten Râmnicu Vâlcea , Drăgășani , Băbeni , Călimănești , Brezoi , Horezu , Berbești , Bălcești und Băile Olănești . ... siehe weitere Olt mit den Städten Slatina , Caracal , Balș , Corabia , Scornicești , Drăgănești-Olt , Piatra-Olt und Potcoava . ... siehe weitere Der größte Fluss der Region ist der Olt , der auch die Grenze zwischen Muntenien und Oltenien bildet. Die Universität Craiova ist eine staatliche Universität in der rumänischen Stadt Craiova mit insgesamt 25.000 Studenten und rund 2.000 wissenschaftlichen Angestellten. Stadtbild und Bauwerke Zu den Sakralen Bauten in der Region gehören die Kirche des Heiligen Demetrius und das Kloster Horezu . Weitere Bauwerke sind unter anderen das Kunstmuseum von Craiova , das Kunstmuseum von Drobeta Turnu Severin , das Hotel Minerva und das Nationaltheater . Mircea I. cel Bătrân (* 1355 ; † 31. Januar 1418 ) war einer der wichtigsten Woiwoden der Walachei . Sein Name bedeutet im modernen Rumänisch „Mircea der Alte“, aber die ursprüngliche Bedeutung des Namens ist „Mircea der Ältere“. Geschichte und Personen Zur Geschichte der Walachei finden sich weitere Artikel zum König Burebista , zur römischen Provinz Dakien , zum Eisernem Tor , zum „ Banat von Severin “, zu Mircea cel Bătrân und zur Vlad III. Drăculea . Zu den bekanntesten Personen der Region gehören Mihai Viteazul , Petrache Poenaru , Theodor Aman , Titu Maiorescu , sowie Alexandru Macedonski . Muzeul de Artă Drobeta Turnu Severin ist ein Kunstmuseum in der Kreishauptstadt Mehedințis Drobeta Turnu Severin . Bildung, Kunst und Wissenschaft Ein breit gefächertes Angebot an Bildungseinrichtungen gibt es in Oltenien für alle Alterstufen. Die Hochschul- und Wissenschaftsregion Oltenien basiert in erster Linie auf der Universität Craiova . Zu den großen Museen in Oltenien gehören das Kunstmuseum von Craiova , das Kunstmuseum von Drobeta Turnu Severin , sowie das Geschichtsmuseum von Caracal .
